all_scores.question: Quais são os modelos de linguagem decoder-only (i.e., GPT-like) voltados para português lançados até final de 2024? Exclua modelos encoder-only (i.e., BERT-like), e encoder-decoder (ex: T5-like). O modelo pode ser público (ex: open-weights na huggingface ou github) ou privado (ex: disponível via API apenas ou apenas descrito em relatório técnico, artigo cientifico, ou blog post). O modelo pode ser apenas um finetuning ou further pretraining de um outro modelo base ou pode ter sido treinado do zero.
all_scores.response:
Below I synthesize the results of the sub-queries into a single, organized answer. I split the output into (A) Portuguese-specific / Portuguese-targeted decoder-only models released by the end of 2024, and (B) major multilingual decoder-only models (GPT-like) that explicitly include Portuguese in their training / support. For each entry I give: model name, release year (or approximate date), developer, whether weights are public or private (API-only or weight download), and whether it was trained from scratch or is a finetune / continued-pretraining of another base model. I also call out notable caveats (license / partial availability / reported-but-not-published sizes).

A. Portuguese-specific / Portuguese-targeted decoder-only models (released by end of 2024)
- Glória (GlorIA) — Glória 1.3B (and checkpoints)
  - Year: 2024
  - Developer: NOVA LINCS / NOVA School (Portugal)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face / repo)
  - Training: native pretraining (decoder-only, pretrained on Portuguese corpus)
  - Caveat: model cards / paper describe dataset and Portuguese focus.

- Gervásio family (multiple sizes reported, HF uploads)
  - Year: 2024
  - Developer: PORTULAN / University of Lisbon (PORTULAN group)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: continued pretraining / finetune of LLaMA-family bases (i.e., adaptation rather than from-scratch)
  - Caveat: multiple variants/sizes across 2024.

- Sabiá (Sabiá-7B; Sabiá paper reports larger 65B)
  - Year: 2023 (paper) / model uploads 2023–2024
  - Developer: Maritaca AI
  - Weights: Sabiá-7B available (Hugging Face); Sabiá-65B reported in paper but not publicly distributed
  - Training: continued pretraining / adaptation of LLaMA-family checkpoints
  - Caveat: some sizes reported in paper are not publicly released.

- Cabrita (open-cabrita3b and family)
  - Year: 2023 (paper) / HF checkpoints 2023–2024
  - Developer: academic / community authors (Cabrita project)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: continued pretraining / tokenizer adaptation from OpenLLaMA / LLaMA-like bases

- Canarim (Canarim-7B and Canarim-7B-Instruct)
  - Year: 2023–2024 (HF uploads updated 2024)
  - Developer: Maicon Domingues / community
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: further pretraining of LLaMA 7B base on Portuguese web data; instruction-tuned variant exists

- Boana-7B-Instruct
  - Year: 2024
  - Developer: community (lrds-code / Leonardo Souza)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: instruction-finetune of LLaMA-based 7B (decoder-only)

- Cabra family (multiple community instruction-finetunes / LoRA)
  - Year: 2023–2024
  - Developer: multiple community contributors (nicolasdec, botbotrobotics, etc.)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face; many LoRA adapters and merged checkpoints)
  - Training: instruction-finetunes / qLoRA / LoRA adapters from LLaMA / Mistral bases

- TeenyTinyLlama (TTL — small native Portuguese models, e.g., TTL-160m, TTL-460m)
  - Year: 2024 (paper + HF/GitHub)
  - Developer: Nicholas Kluge Corrêa et al. (academic / RAIES)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face / GitHub)
  - Training: trained from scratch (small decoder models pretrained on Brazilian Portuguese corpora)

- Aira (Aira-2-portuguese-1B7 and related)
  - Year: 2023–2024
  - Developer: community / nicholaskluge and collaborators
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: finetuned from BLOOM-family or other multilingual base (instruction finetune)

- GPT-2 Portuguese forks (e.g., pierreguillou/gpt2-small-portuguese)
  - Year: community uploads (various years up to 2024)
  - Developer: community contributors
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: finetunes of GPT-2 (decoder-only GPT-2 family)

- Bode (bode-7b-alpaca-pt-br)
  - Year: 2024
  - Developer: Recogna (recogna-nlp)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: instruction-finetuned (LLaMA 2 base → Alpaca-ptbr style SFT / LoRA variants)

- Samba-1.1B
  - Year: 2024
  - Developer: lrds-code / Leonardo Souza
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: fine-tuned / Portuguese-adapted small LLaMA-style model

- Boto (Boto-9B variants)
  - Year: 2024 (HF updates July 2024)
  - Developer: community (lucianosb)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: fine-tuning / Portuguese adaptation of Gemma2-9B-type base

- Clinical-BR-LLaMA-2-7B (medical domain)
  - Year: 2024
  - Developer: HAILab-PUCPR / PUCPR collaborators
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: domain fine-tuning (clinical Portuguese) of LLaMA 2 7B

- Caramelo_7B and other individual community variants
  - Year: 2023–2024
  - Developer: community authors (individual HF users)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)
  - Training: instruction-finetunes / LoRA merges from LLaMA-family bases

- Tucano family (Tucano-1b1, Tucano-3B, Tucano-SFT, etc.)
  - Year: late 2024
  - Developer: TucanoBR / N. Kluge Corrêa and collaborators
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face / GitHub collection)
  - Training: natively pretrained or heavy Portuguese-focused continued pretraining + SFT variants

Notes for the Portuguese-specific list
- Many community Portuguese models are adaptations of LLaMA / LLaMA-2 / OpenLLaMA / Mistral / Gemma / BLOOM bases (i.e., continued pretraining or instruction-finetune), rather than training from zero. A few (TeenyTinyLlama, Tucano variants, Glória) report native pretraining from scratch on Portuguese corpora.
- “Weights public” generally indicates a Hugging Face repo or GitHub checkpoint. Some LLaMA-derived HF uploads are distributed with license restrictions (Meta’s terms) — always check the model card.
- This list includes both monolingual Portuguese models and Portuguese-targeted instruction-finetunes & adapters (LoRA, qLoRA, merged checkpoints). There are many additional small adapters and community LoRAs not enumerated here.

B. Major multilingual decoder-only GPT-like models (released by end of 2024) that include Portuguese
- BLOOM (BigScience)
  - Year: 2022
  - Developer: BigScience / Hugging Face collaborators
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: yes (ROOTS multilingual training; Portuguese among the 46 languages)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)

- BLOOMZ / BLOOMZ instruction-tuned variants
  - Year: 2022–2023
  - Developer: BigScience / community
  - Portuguese included: yes (inherits BLOOM multilingual ability)
  - Weights: public

- XGLM (Meta / Facebook Research)
  - Year: 2021–2022
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: training covers many languages (XGLM model card / paper indicates wide multilingual coverage)
  - Weights: public (model checkpoints on HF / repos)

- GPT-3 / GPT-3.5 / GPT-4 family (OpenAI)
  - Year: 2020–2024 (various releases)
  - Decoder-only: yes (autoregressive)
  - Portuguese included: probable / present in web-based corpora (OpenAI supports Portuguese usage), but OpenAI did not publish per-language pretraining breakdown
  - Weights: private — API-only (no public weights)

- LLaMA family (LLaMA 1 / LLaMA 2 / LLaMA 3)
  - Year: 2023 (LLaMA 1 & 2) / 2024 (LLaMA 3 series)
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: LLaMA families are trained on broad web corpora; LLaMA 3 model cards explicitly list support for Portuguese for some tuned variants; exact per-language breakdown varies
  - Weights: distributed by Meta (weights available subject to license / gated download)

- Falcon family (TII Falcon-7B, Falcon-40B)
  - Year: 2023 (public release Nov 2023)
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: HF model card lists “limited capability” in Portuguese (Falcon supports several languages)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)

- MPT (MosaicML; e.g., MPT-7B)
  - Year: 2023
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: base MPT models are primarily English-centric (not focused on Portuguese)
  - Weights: public

- Pythia (EleutherAI)
  - Year: 2023
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: no (Pythia trained on The Pile — English-dominated)
  - Weights: public

- GPT-Neo / GPT-J / GPT-NeoX
  - Year: 2021–2022
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: not explicitly (trained on The Pile / English-heavy corpora)
  - Weights: public

- StableLM 2 (Stability AI)
  - Year: 2024 (Stable LM 2 announcement)
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: yes (StableLM2 1.6B announcement lists Portuguese among training languages)
  - Weights: public (Hugging Face)

- Mistral family (Mistral 7B, Mistral Large 2)
  - Year: 2023 (Mistral 7B) / 2024 (Mistral Large 2)
  - Decoder-only: yes
  - Portuguese included: Mistral Large 2 specifies support for Portuguese among many languages
  - Weights: public (many Mistral weights available HF / gated licenses)

- Anthropic Claude family
  - Year: 2023–2024 (Claude v1 → Claude 3)
  - Decoder-only: yes (proprietary autoregressive assistant models)
  - Portuguese included: supported in API (multilingual), but no public weights / training breakdown
  - Weights: private (API-only)

- Falcon, BLOOM, LLaMA, Mistral, StableLM2 and similar open-model families are commonly used as bases for Portuguese fine-tunes and adapters (see Section A).

Caveats, coverage & next steps
- The lists above are focused on decoder-only (autoregressive / GPT-like) models that are either Portuguese-specific or multilingual with Portuguese included. I excluded encoder-only (BERT-like) and encoder-decoder (T5-like) models as you requested.
- I included both models trained from scratch on Portuguese text (TeenyTinyLlama, some Tucano/Glória variants) and many community/institutional finetunes (LLaMA → Portuguese variants, LoRAs, instruction-finetunes).
- Availability: “public” indicates downloadable weights / HF repos / GitHub; “private” means API-only or model described in paper/blog but no released weights. Licensing is important: many LLaMA derivatives are distributed under Meta’s LLaMA license or research-only restrictions — check each model card before use.
- This is not an exhaustive catalog of every small LoRA or qLoRA adapter that existed in 2023–2024 (there are dozens); instead I prioritized named Portuguese-targeted decoder-only releases and the major multilingual GPT-style families that include Portuguese.

If you want, I can:

- filter the list to show only models that were trained from scratch (no base reuse) or only instruction-finetunes.

all_scores.question: Quais são os modelos de linguagem decoder-only (i.e., GPT-like) voltados para português lançados até final de 2024? Exclua modelos encoder-only (i.e., BERT-like), e encoder-decoder (ex: T5-like). O modelo pode ser público (ex: open-weights na huggingface ou github) ou privado (ex: disponível via API apenas ou apenas descrito em relatório técnico, artigo cientifico, ou blog post). O modelo pode ser apenas um finetuning ou further pretraining de um outro modelo base ou pode ter sido treinado do zero.
all_scores.response:
Below is a curated, focused list of decoder-only (autoregressive / “GPT-like”) Portuguese language models that were released or publicly described by the end of 2024. I exclude encoder-only (BERT-like) and encoder-decoder (T5-like) models. I include both public releases (weights on Hugging Face / GitHub) and models/projects that were described in papers, reports or announcements but may be API-only or private.

For each entry: name — release date (year or month/year when available) — short description — source link(s) — public vs private status (weights / HF/GitHub vs paper/API).

Note: this is a curated list (representative, not guaranteed exhaustive). Dates are approximate when exact day/month wasn’t given in the source. Many LLaMA-derived models carry the license constraints of their base models — check model cards for license and usage restrictions.

1) Sabiá (Maritaca AI) — Sabiá-7B and family  
- Release: 2023 (family ongoing into 2024)  
- Description: Portuguese-specialized autoregressive models (family includes Sabiá‑7B publicly released; larger variants described in papers/reports). Obtained via continued pretraining / fine-tuning of GPT-J / LLaMA‑style decoders on Portuguese corpora; instruction tuned variants exist.  
- Links: paper/tech report — https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07880 ; HF (Sabiá‑7B) — https://huggingface.co/maritaca-ai/sabia-7b  
- Status: public (Sabiá‑7B) + some larger / commercial variants described

2) Gervásio (PORTULAN / Univ. Lisbon) — Gervasio‑7B / Gervasio‑8B (Portuguese)  
- Release: 2024 (paper / models published in 2024)  
- Description: Decoder LLaMA-family Portuguese models (PT‑BR / PT‑PT variants). Open models and instruction-tuned variants published on HF.  
- Links: paper — https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18766 ; HF — https://huggingface.co/PORTULAN/gervasio-8b-portuguese-ptpt-decoder and https://huggingface.co/PORTULAN/gervasio-7b-portuguese-ptbr-decoder  
- Status: public (HF)

3) GlórIA (NOVA / research) — GlorIA (1.3B, 2.7B reported)  
- Release: 2024  
- Description: Decoder-style generative models targeting European Portuguese (PT‑PT), pre-trained on a large PT‑PT corpus; reported in research outputs.  
- Links: paper — https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12969 ; HF example — https://huggingface.co/NOVA-vision-language/GlorIA-1.3B  
- Status: public (paper + HF assets for some checkpoints)

4) Canarim (community / HF) — Canarim‑7B  
- Release: 2023  
- Description: LLaMA/LLaMA‑2 continued-pretraining / fine-tune targeted to Brazilian Portuguese, with instruction-tuned variants.  
- Link: HF — https://huggingface.co/dominguesm/canarim-7b  
- Status: public (HF)

5) Cabrita (Open Cabrita family / 22-hours) — e.g., Open-Cabrita-3B  
- Release: 2023  
- Description: Portuguese-focused decoder models (e.g., Cabrita 3B), built by continuing pretraining / fine‑tuning LLaMA-style decoders on Portuguese text.  
- Links: repo / info — https://github.com/22-hours/cabrita ; HF — https://huggingface.co/22h/open-cabrita3b  
- Status: public (HF + GitHub)

6) Bode (Recogna / research) — Bode 7B / 13B (Portuguese instruction-tuned variants)  
- Release: 2024 (paper / HF adapters in 2024)  
- Description: LLaMA‑2 based Portuguese instruction / Alpaca-style fine-tuned models (LoRA / full fine-tunes) for PT‑BR; described in a 2024 paper.  
- Links: paper — https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02909 ; HF examples — https://huggingface.co/recogna-nlp/bode-7b-alpaca-pt-br and https://huggingface.co/recogna-nlp/bode-13b-alpaca-pt-br  
- Status: public (HF adapters / fine-tunes) + paper

7) TeenyTinyLlama (TTL) / Samba (Nicholas Kluge Corrêa et al.) — small PT‑BR decoder LLMs  
- Release: 2024 (preprint and model releases around Jan 2024)  
- Description: Small autoregressive LLaMA-like models trained for Brazilian Portuguese (range: ~160M–1.1B in reported collections such as Samba 1.1B and TTL family). Released code / weights for some sizes.  
- Links: paper — https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16640 ; HF collection — https://huggingface.co/collections/nicholasKluge/teenytinyllama-6582ea8129e72d1ea4d384f1 ; Samba HF — https://huggingface.co/lrds-code/samba-1.1B  
- Status: public (HF + GitHub)

8) Caramelo (community) — Caramelo_7B (Falcon-based / decoder)  
- Release: 2023 (HF model card activity)  
- Description: Falcon‑7B-based causal model fine-tuned for Portuguese (community release / fine-tune). Decoder-only since Falcon is an autoregressive model.  
- Link: HF — https://huggingface.co/Bruno/Caramelo_7B  
- Status: public (HF)

9) GPorTuguese / GPT-2 Portuguese adaptations (community)  
- Release: early (2020+) for GPT-2 fine-tunes, ongoing community versions through 2022–2024  
- Description: GPT-2 small / GPT-Neo style causal models fine-tuned for Portuguese (community baseline generation models).  
- Example link: https://huggingface.co/pierreguillou/gpt2-small-portuguese  
- Status: public (HF)

10) GPT2-Bio-PT (HAILab / PUCPR)  
- Release: 2021 (repo/paper dates)  
- Description: Biomedical domain fine‑tune of GPT‑2 for Portuguese clinical/biomedical text — decoder-only.  
- Link: GitHub — https://github.com/HAILab-PUCPR/gpt2-bio-pt  
- Status: public (GitHub)

11) Carious community Alpaca/Alpaca-LoRA PT‑BR forks and adapters (many HF releases 2023–2024)  
- Release: 2023–2024 (multiple community releases)  
- Description: Instruction-tuned, LoRA or full-fine-tune adapters applied to LLaMA / LLaMA‑2 / Falcon decoders to create PT‑BR instruction-following models (commonly called “Alpaca-PTBR” etc.). These are decoder-only by construction.  
- Example HF: https://huggingface.co/dominguesm/alpaca-lora-ptbr-7b  
- Status: public (HF)

12) AMÁLIA (Portuguese national LLM initiative) — announced Nov 2024  
- Release / announcement: Nov 2024 (project announced)  
- Description: National LLM initiative in Portugal to produce a Portuguese-focused large model (project announcement and technical descriptions made public by end of 2024). At announcement time, model details and weights were planned / described but full model release proceeded after end of 2024. Included because it is explicitly a Portuguese-focused decoder LLM initiative.  
- Links: project site / govt announcement — https://amaliallm.pt/ ; https://www.portugal.gov.pt/pt/gc24/comunicacao/noticia?i=modelo-de-linguagem-em-grande-escala-para-a-lingua-portuguesa ; Wikipedia (summary) — https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%A1lia_(LLM)  
- Status: announced / partly-public info (not necessarily public weights by end of 2024)

Other notes and caveats
- Many Portuguese LLMs are community derivatives (LoRA, adapters, fine‑tunes) of multilingual bases (LLaMA, LLaMA‑2, GPT‑Neo, Falcon, GPT‑J). I included the community fine-tunes and small dedicated Portuguese models above because they are decoder-only by architecture.  
- Some large Portuguese-branded models (e.g., larger Sabiá variants, Maritaca commercial models, or national initiatives) had API-only or private releases; I included them when they were publicly described by end of 2024.  
- Licenses, usage restrictions and exact parameter counts vary across models — check each model card / repo before use. LLaMA-derived models often inherit license restrictions from Meta.  
- This list focuses on models explicitly targeted at Portuguese (PT-PT or PT-BR). Multilingual decoder models (e.g., GPT-NeoX multilingual releases) are not listed unless a Portuguese-focused checkpoint / fine-tune exists.

Below is a focused, curated inventory of decoder-only (autoregressive / “GPT‑like”) language models that target Portuguese and were publicly announced or documented by the end of 2024. I include both models trained from scratch and Portuguese-specific fine-tunes / continued-pretraining of base decoder models, and I note whether weights were publicly released or only accessible via API/paper. I exclude encoder-only and encoder–decoder models.

For each item: name — release (month/year or year) — decoder-only? — weights public? — trained from scratch or finetune/base — representative sizes (when applicable) — authoritative source(s).

Key Portuguese-specific decoder-only models

- Gervásio (PORTULAN)
  - Release: 2024 (paper/announcement Feb 2024; HF model cards through 2024)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (causal autoregressive; LLaMA-family architecture)
  - Weights: Public — model cards and checkpoints on Hugging Face (safetensors/GGUF for several variants)
  - Training: continued pretraining / instruction tuning from LLaMA-family checkpoints
  - Sizes: examples: 7B, 8B, 70B variants reported
  - Sources: arXiv paper (Feb 2024) https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18766 ; HF model cards (examples) https://huggingface.co/PORTULAN/gervasio-7b-portuguese-ptpt-decoder , https://huggingface.co/PORTULAN/gervasio-70b-portuguese-ptpt-decoder

  - Release: 2024 (preprint Nov 2024; HF + repo releases in 2024)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (causal LM / GPT-like)
  - Weights: Public — models, code and dataset released on Hugging Face & GitHub
  - Training: trained from scratch / native pretraining on a curated Portuguese corpus (GigaVerbo)
  - Sizes: multiple (examples in the release: 160M, 630M, ~1.1B, ~2.4B)
  - Sources: arXiv (Nov 2024) https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07854 ; HF collection https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR ; project repo/website https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/ and https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano

- Sabiá family (Maritaca AI)

    - Release: 2023 (model card / HF upload in 2023)
    - Decoder-only: Yes (LLaMA-style causal)
    - Weights: Public (Hugging Face model card exists; distribution subject to base-model license)
    - Training: continued pretraining from LLaMA-1 7B checkpoint (per model card / paper)
    - Source: HF model card https://huggingface.co/maritaca-ai/sabia-7b ; Sabiá paper (2023) https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07880
  - Sabiá‑3 (flagship reported 2024)
    - Release: technical report published Oct 2024
    - Decoder-only: Yes
    - Weights: Not openly downloadable as of end‑2024 — available via Maritaca API / product rather than public checkpoint
    - Training: further pretraining + instruction alignment described in Sabiá‑3 report
    - Source: technical report (Oct 2024) https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12049 ; Maritaca AI pages https://www.maritaca.ai/

- GlórIA (NOVA)
  - Release: 2024 (PROPOR 2024 paper; HF upload in 2024)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (GPT‑Neo style / causal LM)
  - Weights: Public (Hugging Face model card)
  - Training: trained on a large European‑Portuguese corpus (native Portuguese pretraining)
  - Sizes: GlórIA‑1.3B (documented)
  - Sources: PROPOR 2024 paper / ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2024.propor-1.45/ ; HF repo https://huggingface.co/NOVA-vision-language/GlorIA-1.3B ; GitHub https://github.com/rvlopes/GlorIA

- TeenyTinyLlama (TTL)
  - Release: 2024 (arXiv Jan 2024; HF & GitHub releases in 2024)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (LLaMA-style causal small models)
  - Weights: Public (GitHub + Hugging Face)

  - Sizes: examples ~160M, ~460M
  - Sources: arXiv (Jan 2024) https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16640 ; GitHub https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/TeenyTinyLlama ; HF examples (e.g., https://huggingface.co/nicholasKluge/TeenyTinyLlama-460m)

  - Release: 2023 (paper Aug 2023; HF openCabrita uploads 2023/2024)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (OpenLLaMA / LLaMA-style)
  - Weights: Public (HF model cards / community uploads)
  - Training: continued pretraining / adaptation for Portuguese using open LLaMA bases
  - Sizes: openCabrita 3B (example)
  - Sources: Cabrita paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11878 ; HF example https://huggingface.co/22h/open-cabrita3b

Notable earlier / community Portuguese decoder-only models and fine-tunes (representative examples)

- GPT-2 Portuguese fine-tunes (community)
  - Release: from 2020 onwards (community uploads)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (GPT‑2 causal)
  - Weights: Public (Hugging Face model cards)
  - Training: fine-tuned from GPT‑2 on Portuguese corpora (Wikipedia, Common Crawl subsets, community corpora)
  - Examples & HF model cards:
    - pierreguillou/gpt2-small-portuguese (GPT‑2 small fine‑tuned) https://huggingface.co/pierreguillou/gpt2-small-portuguese
    - other community GPT‑2 fine‑tunes searchable on HF (tag: Portuguese / pt)

- Community LLaMA / LLaMA‑2 / Mistral / Falcon Portuguese finetunes (community-made PT models)
  - Release: 2023–2024 (many community uploads)
  - Decoder-only: Yes (base LLaMA/Mistral/Falcon are decoder-only)
  - Weights: Public (community HF uploads)
  - Training: fine‑tuned or instruction‑tuned from base LLaMA / Mistral / Falcon weights to Portuguese
  - Representative examples:
    - recogna-nlp/bode-7b-alpaca-pt-br (LLaMA‑2 → Portuguese Alpaca‑style SFT) https://huggingface.co/recogna-nlp/bode-7b-alpaca-pt-br
    - rhaymison/Llama-portuguese-13b-Luana-v0.2 (LLaMA-based Portuguese model) https://huggingface.co/rhaymison/Llama-portuguese-13b-Luana-v0.2
    - cnmoro/Mistral-7B-Portuguese (community Mistral → PT) https://huggingface.co/cnmoro/Mistral-7B-Portuguese

- Tucano / TeenyTinyLlama / Gervásio / GlórIA above are the main research / project releases that targeted Portuguese specifically with public artifacts in 2024. Sabiá examples combine public smaller models (7B) with a larger Sabiá‑3 described in a 2024 technical report but provided via API rather than as open checkpoints.

Multilingual decoder-only models that include Portuguese (context)
- Several large multilingual decoder-only models (BLOOM, mGPT, GPT‑J, GPT‑NeoX, LLaMA and LLaMA‑2, Falcon, Mistral, MPT, XGen) were publicly released by end of 2024 and natively include Portuguese text in their pretraining mixes. They are not Portuguese‑only models, but many community Portuguese finetunes/instruction variants were built on them — examples and links given above on request. (If you want, I can list all community Portuguese finetunes for each base.)

Notes, caveats and licensing
- “Public” here means a checkpoint or HF model card was available for download on Hugging Face / GitHub by 2024‑12‑31. Some models are available but inherit restrictive base-model licenses (e.g., LLaMA-derived models or models trained on restricted data), so check the model card license / allowed uses.

- I focused on models that explicitly target Portuguese (monolingual Portuguese or Portuguese-specific finetunes). There are many multilingual decoders that support Portuguese to varying degrees — I can add a separate section listing prominent multilingual decoders and any official Portuguese-targeted finetunes.

Summary — DLC Remembrance bosses and their trade rewards (Shadow of the Erdtree)

Notes up front
- All DLC Remembrances are exchanged at Finger Reader Enia in the Roundtable Hold (Enia’s “Receive power from Remembrance” menu).  
- For each Remembrance you get a choice of one (1) item from Enia’s menu, or you can instead consume / sell the Remembrance for runes (value shown). To obtain both Enia items from a single Remembrance in one playthrough you must duplicate the Remembrance (e.g., Remembrance Duplication Coffin / Walking Mausoleum) and trade duplicates separately.
- Below I list each DLC remembrance, the exact in‑game Remembrance name, the trade items Enia offers (exact names as commonly listed in guides), and the rune amount if you consume/sell the Remembrance.

1) Divine Beast Dancing Lion
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Dancing Lion
- Enia trade options:
  - Enraged Divine Beast (talisman)
  - Ash of War: Divine Beast Frost Stomp (Ash of War)
- Consume / sell: 30,000 Runes

2) Rellana, Twin Moon Knight
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Twin Moon Knight
- Enia trade options:
  - Rellana’s Twin Blades
  - Rellana’s Twin Moons
- Consume / sell: 30,000 Runes

3) Messmer the Impaler
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Impaler
- Enia trade options:
  - Spear of the Impaler (weapon)
  - Messmer’s Orb (incantation)
- Consume / sell: 40,000 Runes

4) Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Lord of Frenzied Flame
- Enia trade options:
  - Greatsword of Damnation (weapon)
  - Midra’s Flame of Frenzy (incantation)
- Consume / sell: 40,000 Runes

5) Putrescent Knight
- Remembrance: Remembrance of Putrescence
- Enia trade options:
  - Putrescence Cleaver (weapon)
  - Vortex of Putrescence (sorcery)
- Consume / sell: 30,000 Runes

6) Scadutree Avatar
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower
- Enia trade options:
  - Shadow Sunflower Blossom
  - Land of Shadow (incantation)
- Consume / sell: 40,000 Runes

7) Commander Gaius (Wild Boar Rider)
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider
- Enia trade options:
  - Sword Lance (weapon)
  - Blades of Stone (sorcery)
- Consume / sell: 30,000 Runes

8) Romina, Saint of the Bud
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Saint of the Bud
- Enia trade options:
  - Poleblade of the Bud (weapon)
  - Rotten Butterflies
- Consume / sell: 30,000 Runes

9) Metyr, the Mother of Fingers
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Mother of Fingers
- Enia trade options:
  - Staff of the Great Beyond (staff/weapon)
  - Gazing Finger
- Consume / sell: 40,000 Runes

10) Radahn, Consort of Miquella (DLC final boss)
- Remembrance: Remembrance of a God and a Lord
- Enia trade options:
  - Greatsword of Radahn (Lord)*
  - Greatsword of Radahn (Light)* 
  - Light of Miquella (incantation)
- Consume / sell: 50,000 Runes

(*The Radahn remembrance presents multiple prominent weapon/light options — the above lists the common named rewards shown in DLC guides.)

all_scores.question: Você pode fazer um relatório sobre todos os chefes de lembrança de Elden Ring considerando apenas o jogo base? Quero saber todas as recompensas que podem ser trocadas por cada lembrança.
all_scores.response:
Below is a concise report of every base‑game Elden Ring boss that drops a Remembrance (no DLC bosses), and the two unique rewards you can trade that Remembrance for with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold. I list the boss, the Remembrance name, the two Enia trade choices (exact in‑game names) and a short note on the reward type/what it does.

Notes up front
- Trade location: Finger Reader Enia, Roundtable Hold — choose “Receive power from remembrance.”  
- Each Remembrance gives two mutually exclusive choices; once redeemed the Remembrance is consumed. To take both choices in one playthrough you must duplicate the Remembrance first (Walking Mausoleums / duplication mechanics).  
- I include only base‑game bosses and their in‑game trade rewards.

1) Godrick the Grafted  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Grafted  
- Trade choices:
  - Axe of Godrick — Weapon (Greataxe). Godrick’s unique heavy axe weapon with its special skill and Somber smithing upgrade path.  
  - Grafted Dragon — Weapon (Fist-type / dragon-themed weapon). Unique, fire‑themed graft weapon with a dragon/breath effect; upgradeable with Somber Smithing Stones.

2) Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen  
- Trade choices:
  - Carian Regal Scepter — Glintstone Staff. Unique staff tied to Rennala/Carian Sorceries (Intelligence scaling).  
  - Rennala’s Full Moon — Sorcery. Rennala’s signature full‑moon sorcery (offensive sorcery with area/effect).

3) Starscourge Radahn  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Starscourge  
- Trade choices:
  - Starscourge Greatsword — Weapon (Greatsword/colossal paired weapon). Radahn’s unique heavy sword with special skill/gravitic flavor.  
  - Lion Greatbow — Weapon (Greatbow). Radahn’s unique greatbow with a special arrow rain skill.

4) Regal Ancestor Spirit  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Regal Ancestor  
- Trade choices:
  - Winged Greathorn — Weapon (Greataxe/horn weapon). Unique greataxe themed on the ancestral spirit.  
  - Ancestral Spirit's Horn — Talisman / Tool effect. A horn/talisman‑type reward tied to ancestral spirit effects (restoration/FP on certain events).

5) Morgott, the Omen King  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Omen King  
- Trade choices:
  - Morgott’s Cursed Sword — Weapon (Curved Greatsword / boss weapon). Morgott’s unique sword with its special skill and bleed/arcane flavor.  
  - Regal Omen Bairn — Tool (spirit doll summoning/tool). A reusable tool that summons wraiths/omen‑bairns to attack foes.

6) Astel, Naturalborn of the Void  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Naturalborn  
- Trade choices:
  - Bastard’s Stars — Weapon (flail / boss weapon). A star‑themed weapon with magic damage elements and unique moveset.  
  - Ash of War: Waves of Darkness — Ash of War. Grants the Waves of Darkness skill (darkness‑wave attack); usable on compatible armaments.

7) Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Blasphemous  
- Trade choices:
  - Blasphemous Blade — Weapon (Greatsword). Rykard’s unique greatsword with fire/blood‑flame effects and life‑steal/healing interactions.  
  - Rykard’s Rancor — Incantation / Sorcery‑like offensive skill (fire/magma theme). Ranged/fire attack tied to Rykard’s power.

8) Lichdragon Fortissax  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Lichdragon  
- Trade choices:
  - Fortissax’s Lightning Spear — Incantation. Powerful dragon/lightning incantation summoning spear strikes (large lightning damage).  
  - Death Lightning — Incantation. Corrupted/Death‑type lightning spell that can apply Death Blight and large lightning AoE.

9) Fire Giant  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Fire Giant  
- Trade choices:
  - Giant’s Red Braid — Weapon. Fire Giant‑themed heavy weapon (braided whip/large weapon) with fire properties and unique skill.  
  - Burn, O Flame! — Incantation. A strong area‑of‑effect fire incantation summoning pillars/flames.

10) Mohg, Lord of Blood  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Blood Lord  
- Trade choices:
  - Mohgwyn’s Sacred Spear — Weapon (Great Spear). Mohg’s signature spear with blood/hemorrhage effects and a unique skill.  
  - Bloodboon — Incantation. Mohg blood incantation that creates pools/area bloodflame and applies hemorrhage buildup.

11) Maliketh, the Black Blade  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Black Blade  
- Trade choices:
  - Maliketh’s Black Blade — Weapon (Colossal Sword). Maliketh’s unique blade with death/destined‑death theme and special skill.  
  - Black Blade — Incantation (or special skill variant). A death/destined‑death type spell/ability tied to Maliketh’s power.

12) Dragonlord Placidusax  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Dragonlord  
- Trade choices:
  - Dragon King’s Cragblade — Weapon. Placidusax’s unique piercing/heavy blade with dragon/lighting flavor.  
  - Placidusax’s Ruin — Incantation / Dragon skill. Transformative dragon/area attack tied to the Dragonlord theme.

13) Hoarah Loux (Godfrey’s second phase / Hoarah Loux, Warrior)  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of Hoarah Loux  
- Trade choices:
  - Axe of Godfrey — Weapon (Colossal greataxe). Hoarah/Godfrey’s heavy greataxe with unique skill and Somber upgrade path.  
  - Ash of War: Hoarah Loux’s Earthshaker — Ash of War. Grants the Earthshaker skill (shockwave slam) to compatible weapons.

14) Malenia, Goddess of Rot  
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Rot Goddess  
- Trade choices:
  - Hand of Malenia — Weapon (Katana / prosthetic blade). Malenia’s prosthetic blade with Waterfowl Dance skill and strong bleed potential.  
  - Scarlet Aeonia — Incantation / Spell. Summons a giant scarlet blossom that explodes and inflicts heavy Scarlet Rot buildup.

15) Elden Beast  
- Remembrance: Elden Remembrance  
- Trade choices:
  - Marika’s Hammer — Weapon (Hammer). Marika’s hammer/unique weapon with holy/physical damage and special skill.  
  - Sacred Relic Sword — Weapon (Greatsword). A holy greatsword forged from divine remains with physical + holy damage and unique skill.

If you’d like, I can:
- Produce this as a table sorted by boss location, by reward type, or grouped by weapons/spells/Ashes.  
- Add the exact rune values for consuming each Remembrance (alternate to trading).  
- Show where to duplicate each Remembrance so you can pick both options in one playthrough.

all_scores.response:
Below is a consolidated report of all Nightlord bosses in Elden Ring: Nightreign (base + Forsaken Hollows DLC) and the unique relic(s) awarded the first time you defeat each Nightlord. For each boss I give: 1) full boss name + where/when encountered, 2) short description + main mechanics, 3) unique relic(s) awarded on first clear (name + summarized in‑game effect), and 4) source link(s). Effects are summarized — if you want exact numeric values I can fetch them from the relic pages.

Summary — Nightlord bosses (10 total)
- Base game Nightlords (8): Gladius (Tricephalos), Adel (Baron of Night), Gnoster (Wisdom of Night), Maris (Fathom of Night), Libra (Creature of Night), Fulghor (Champion of Nightglow), Caligo (Miasma of Night), Heolstor (the Nightlord / Night Aspect).
- Forsaken Hollows (DLC) Nightlords (2): Weapon‑Bequeathed Harmonia (Balancers), Traitorous Straghess (Dreglord).

Details per Nightlord

1) Gladius, Beast of Night (Tricephalos)
- Encounter: Tricephalos expedition — Nightlord fight on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Three‑headed, multi‑legged beast that can split into smaller hounds. Heavy melee bites and sweeping attacks, flame breath, later splits/swarm phase and powerful recombined attacks. Telegraphed swings; vulnerable windows when splitting/recombining.
- Unique relic(s) on first clear:
  - Night of the Beast — green relic. Summary effect: grants stamina/attack-related benefits (stamina recovery on hits and fire damage with starting armament — see relic page for exact numbers).
  - Old Pocketwatch — (also listed as a reward from this run). Summary: FP restoration on successive attacks and stat bonuses (see page for exact values).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius+Beast+of+Night
  - Relics: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Beast and https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Old+Pocketwatch

2) Adel, Baron of Night
- Encounter: Gaping Jaw expedition — Nightlord on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Large drake/dragon‑style Nightlord with powerful jaw attacks, charges and later lightning/area fissures and aerial dives in later phases. Strong single‑target and area zoning abilities.
- Unique relic (first clear):
  - Night of the Baron — blue relic. Summary effect: improves critical-related benefits and recovery interactions (boosts criticals and related gauges; see page for exact mechanics).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Adel+Baron+of+Night
  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Baron

3) Gnoster, Wisdom of Night
- Encounter: Sentient Pest expedition — Nightlord on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Multi‑component encounter involving a flying moth and a scorpion‑like partner sharing a bar. Projectile magic, poison/mist, pincers/stomps and combined/possession phases; can split or revive in variants.
- Unique relic (first clear):
  - Night of the Wise — yellow relic. Summary effect: increases maximum FP and grants poison-related offensive benefits (starting armament inflicts Poison; FP increases; other Poison/Rot interaction bonuses).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gnoster+Wisdom+of+Night
  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Wise

4) Maris, Fathom of Night
- Encounter: Augur expedition — Nightlord on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Floating, octopus/squid‑like Nightlord using water/wave/gust attacks, tentacle strikes, summons (exploding jellyfish) and phase blasts. Hypnosis/Sleep mechanics in some attacks; susceptible to Lightning.
- Unique relic (first clear):
  - Night of the Fathom — red relic. Summary effect: raises max HP and grants expedition/healing synergies (flask/allied healing interactions and other HP-related benefits).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Maris+Fathom+of+Night
  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Fathom

5) Libra, Creature of Night
- Encounter: Equilibrious Beast expedition — Nightlord on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Goat‑headed demon that uses quarterstaff combos, light/glyph projectiles and a meditation mechanic (sigils to interrupt). Deals with Madness mechanics and has merchant/deal pre‑fight options in the expedition.
- Unique relic (first clear):
  - Night of the Demon — red relic. Summary effect: grants shop/expedition discounts and madness/FP interaction bonuses (e.g., gestures/building Madness gives FP regeneration and other perks; see page for full details).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Libra+Creature+of+Night
  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Demon

- Encounter: Darkdrift Knight expedition — Nightlord on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Centaur/knight with lance and charge moves; fast thrusts, ground sweep shockwaves and, in later phases, added summoned arm/slam attacks and golden area attacks.
- Unique relic (first clear):
  - Night of the Champion — green relic. Summary effect: increases maximum stamina and enhances guard/counter/thrust interactions (guard counter damage and HP‑related recovery on certain counters).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fulghor+Champion+of+Nightglow
  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Champion

- Unique relic (first clear):

  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/The+Will+of+the+Balancers

10) Traitorous Straghess (Dreglord) — (Forsaken Hollows DLC)
- Encounter: Dreglord expedition (Forsaken Hollows DLC) — Nightlord on Day 3 (Night 3).
- Short description / mechanics: Massive composite corpse fiend with staff/arm slams, scarlet rot zoning, summons of putrid corpses and explosive flesh pools. Multiple phases including fast, erratic final transformations and high Rot pressure.
- Unique relic (first clear, DLC):
  - The Night of Dregs — red relic. Summary effect: rot/dreg‑themed bonuses tied to Scarlet Rot interactions and expedition effects (see relic page for exact mechanics).
- Source:
  - Boss page: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Traitorous+Straghess
  - Relic: https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/The+Night+of+Dregs

Notes, caveats and next steps
- Sources used: the Nightreign/Wiki pages on Fextralife (linked above) were the primary sources for boss descriptions and relic names/effect summaries. Those pages in turn cite in‑game drops and community testing. If you want I can cross‑reference each relic’s exact numeric values (HP/FP/stamina modifiers, % boosts, cooldowns) with the relic pages or the Elden Ring wiki (eldenring.wiki.gg) and list the numbers precisely.

all_scores.question: Você pode fazer um relatório sobre todos os chefes Nightlord de Elden Ring Nightreign? Também quero saber todas as relíquias únicas obtidas ao derrotar cada Nightlord pela primeira vez.
all_scores.response:
Below is a consolidated report on all Nightlord bosses in Elden Ring: Nightreign and the unique relic(s) you obtain when you defeat each Nightlord for the first time. I list each boss (canonical in‑game name), where the encounter appears (expedition), a short fight summary, primary weakness/affinity to exploit, then the unique relic awarded on first clear (name + short description / how to obtain). At the end I summarize Everdark / DLC caveats.

Summary totals
- Base Nightreign Nightlords: 8
- Forsaken Hollows (DLC) Nightlords: 2
- Grand total Nightlord bosses covered: 10

1) Gladius, Beast of Night
- Expedition / encounter: Tricephalos expedition (Tricephalos — Gladius, Beast of Night)
- Short fight summary: Fast, three‑headed wolf with a long chained sword. Alternates between a single Tricephalos form and a split trio form (one sword‑wolf + two smaller wolves). Split form increases mobility and swarm pressure; recombine windows are key openings.
- Primary weakness: Holy affinity is especially effective; status procs Bleed/Frostbite also work well.
- Unique relics on first defeat:
  - Night of the Beast — boss relic (Green slot). Flavor: “the night belonging to Gladius…”. Effects: stamina / on‑hit / fire infusion style passive (community/tooltip summaries list stamina/FIRE related passives). Awarded on first successful Tricephalos clear.
  - Old Pocketwatch — guaranteed key/unique relic on first clear. Effects summary: FP/skill utility and a small Dexterity stat bump (community summaries). Obtained as guaranteed first‑clear reward.

2) Adel, Baron of Night
- Expedition / encounter: Gaping Jaw expedition
- Short fight summary: Large drake/dragon with devastating jaw bites, charges and (in later phase) lightning AoE and fissures. Poison is especially effective in Phase 1 (stagger/interrupt); Everdark variant adds teleports / more aggressive lightning.
- Primary weakness: Poison is the single most reliable exploit (creates long openings). Also Frostbite/Scarlet Rot have value in some contexts.
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - Night of the Baron — boss relic (Blue slot). Effects: passive critical/crit‑related bonuses (community summaries list improved criticals, art gauge fill on crit, etc.). Awarded as the first‑clear unique relic. (Defeating the Everdark Sovereign Adel unlocks a Dark Night of the Baron variant available via Collector Signboard.)

3) Gnoster, Wisdom of Night (Sentient Pest)
- Expedition / encounter: Sentient Pest expedition
- Short fight summary: Two‑body encounter (large scorpion + a large moth) sharing one HP pool; the moth handles flying/magic projectiles and parasite/poison, scorpion handles heavy physical attacks. Phase transitions combine their attacks into dangerous paired patterns.
- Primary weakness: Fire affinity is the clearest damage advantage (bring ranged for the moth).
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - Night of the Wise — boss relic (Yellow slot). Effects: increases max FP and confers poison application on starting armament, plus poison/rot synergy effects (community summaries). Granted as a first‑clear unique relic.

4) Maris, Fathom of Night (Augur)
- Expedition / encounter: Augur expedition
- Short fight summary: Floating/hovering, summons jellyfish/minions and uses a large Hypnosis (Sleep) channel that must be interrupted. Uses falling teardrop bombs and tentacle/wave attacks; the fight rewards Lightning interrupts and detonating summoned minions near Maris.
- Primary weakness: Lightning affinity (best for interrupting Hypnosis and staggering).
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - Night of the Fathom — boss relic. Effects: increases maximum HP and grants ally/healing / team utility (e.g., flask heals allies or ally‑oriented effects), making it useful for co‑op. Awarded as the first clear reward (Everdark variant gives a “Dark Night of the Fathom” purchasable from Collector Signboard after defeating the Everdark Sovereign).

5) Libra, Creature of Night (Equilibrious Beast)
- Expedition / encounter: Equilibrious Beast expedition
- Short fight summary: Goat‑headed staff wielder that places glyphs/sigils, uses ranged Madness/Golden‑Order projectiles and has a meditation/shield mechanic: if you interrupt meditation you get a dangerous but vulnerable melee berserk; if you let it finish it becomes projectile‑heavy and defensive.
- Primary weakness: Madness mechanics are Libra’s key exploitable element — applying Madness forces a vulnerable frenzy melee state. Holy and Fire are useful secondary choices.
- Unique relic acquisition note:
  - Dark Night of the Demon (often shown as Night of the Demon / Dark Night of the Demon) — this Everdark variant relic becomes available for purchase from the Collector Signboard after you defeat the Everdark Sovereign variant (Everdark Libra). The base (non‑Everdark) Libra encounter does not automatically grant that unique Everdark relic; defeating the Everdark Sovereign unlocks the signboard purchase (commonly costs Sovereign Sigils). In short: to obtain the special Libra relic you must beat the Everdark Sovereign variant and then buy it from the Collector Signboard.

6) Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow (Darkdrift Knight)
- Expedition / encounter: Darkdrift Knight expedition
- Short fight summary: Mobile lance/cavalier boss (centaur‑like) with lance thrusts, golden lance channeling (spawns pillars), charges that leave explosive trails. Lightning works well to interrupt his Golden Lance channel; phase transition gives good punishment windows.
- Primary weakness: Lightning affinity (interrupts his big channel moves); Poison/Scarlet Rot can help chip when mobile.
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - Night of the Champion — boss relic (Green slot). Effects: stamina/guard counter / thrust/counter play bonuses (community summaries). Awarded on first clear. (Defeating the Everdark Sovereign variant later unlocks a Dark Night of the Champion in the Collector Signboard.)

7) Caligo, Miasma of Night (Fissure in the Fog)
- Expedition / encounter: Fissure in the Fog expedition
- Short fight summary: Draconic Nightlord that uses frost breath, aerial dive barrages and fog/mist that obscures vision. It scatters frost hazards and Frostbite crystals; fight requires careful positioning and gap‑closing to attack hind legs/underbody.
- Primary weakness: Fire affinity is strongly effective (fire hits can stagger / reduce attack & defense temporarily).
- Unique relic acquisition note:
  - Dark Night of the Miasma / Night of the Miasma (community naming varies) — community sources indicate defeating Caligo unlocks access to the relic (it commonly becomes purchasable from the Collector Signboard after clearing the encounter). Check your Collector Signboard after first clear to obtain/purchase the relic (Sovereign Sigils may be required depending on variant). Everdark variant details may alter availability or provide a Dark variant.

8) Heolstor the Nightlord (encounter initially appears as "Shape of Night")
- Expedition / encounter: Night Aspect expedition (appears initially as Shape of Night; true form revealed as Heolstor)
- Short fight summary: Two‑stage reveal: begin vs Shape of Night, then Heolstor the Nightlord appears — highly aggressive greatsword wielder who imbues attacks with different elements/statuses and creates arena fissures (Night of the Lord / rift slam). Many elemental/status infusions (Fire/Lightning/Holy/Poison/Frost/Sleep/Madness) in later slams.
- Primary weakness: Holy affinity is specially effective; Holy helps stagger and open windows.
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - Night of the Lord — boss relic (Blue slot). Effects: Weapon switching grants a temporary affinity infusion and attack boost when switching (i.e., switching weapons adds an affinity attack / boosts those attacks). Awarded on first clear of the Night Aspect (Heolstor).

9) Weapon‑Bequeathed Harmonia (Forsaken Hollows DLC — Balancers)
- Expedition / encounter: Balancers expedition (Forsaken Hollows DLC)
- Short fight summary: Multi‑body boss comprised of seven Balancer valkyrie‑like spearfighters sharing a global health pool. Phase 1: kill lesser Balancers; Phase 2: they revive with a leader and coordinated, synchronized dive/spear rains. Sleep status is particularly strong (they fall asleep quickly).
- Primary weakness: Sleep is the best single exploit (Sleep weapons/inflictions make the fight much easier).
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - The Will of the Balancers — unique boss relic (Blue slot). Effects summary: melee and skill/ability attack boosts and FP recovery passives (community summaries list +melee/skill% and steady FP regen). This is a DLC boss — must own Forsaken Hollows to face it; relic awarded on first clear.

10) Traitorous Straghess (Dreglord — Forsaken Hollows DLC)
- Expedition / encounter: Dreglord expedition (Forsaken Hollows DLC)
- Short fight summary: Huge composite corpse mound with staff slams and heavy Scarlet Rot mechanics; transforms into a faster, more aggressive Pure Impulse Straghess for a second health bar. The fight centers on heavy rot hazard management and adds.
- Primary weakness: No single elemental soft spot — the fight is about rot mitigation and raw DPS; bring rot cures and be mobile.
- Unique relic on first defeat:
  - The Night of Dregs — unique boss relic (Red slot). Effects: encourages ailment/rot builds (attack buffs while afflicted and rot‑synergy healing/bonuses; community summaries show stacking attack power while afflicted and rot‑area healing). Awarded on first successful defeat of Traitorous Straghess. (Dreglord access requires Forsaken Hollows and expedition chain progression.)

Everdark Sovereign variants / Collector Signboard notes (general)
- Many Nightlords have enhanced Everdark Sovereign variants (event or late content) that either:
  - Drop different “Dark Night of …” relic variants, or
  - Unlock a special “Dark Night …” relic for purchase from the Collector Signboard after you defeat that Everdark Sovereign variant once.
- Practically: some relics are given directly on the first clear (most base bosses), but in several cases the Everdark variant yields an alternate “Dark” relic that you must buy from the Collector Signboard once that Everdark boss has been defeated. Check the Collector Signboard after beating Everdark variants for additional purchasable relics (usually priced with Sovereign Sigils).

Notes & caveats
- The descriptions above synthesize community guides, Nightreign wiki/tooltips and player reports. Exact relic tooltips and numeric values (e.g., +HP, +stamina, percent boosts) are best checked in‑game or on a current Nightreign database because some relics have variable rolls or different numeric values across patches or Everdark variants.
- Where community sources differed on whether a relic is handed directly as the free first‑clear reward or unlocked as a purchase at the Collector Signboard after an Everdark clear, I summarized the common, confirmed acquisition route (first‑clear direct reward vs. post‑Everdark signboard purchase). If you want, I can pull and paste the exact in‑game flavor text and precise numeric values for each relic from the current Nightreign wiki pages.

Do you want:
- A printable one‑page boss card per Nightlord (telegraphs, tells, priority counters)?
- The exact in‑game relic tooltip text (verbatim) and numeric values for each relic?
- Recommended loadouts/gear and relic pairings for solo vs 3‑player co‑op for any particular boss?

I include source links for each entry.

1) Gladius, Beast of Night (a.k.a. Tricephalos)  
- Short description: Three‑headed, bestial Nightlord with fast multi‑headed slashes, lunges and fire/AoE attacks; fights force you to manage simultaneous threats from several heads.  
- First‑clear relic(s): Night of the Beast (unique relic) — plus the Old Pocketwatch key/keepsake is granted on first clear. (Immediate first‑clear rewards.)  
- Main weakness: Holy (primary).  
- Sources: Fextralife / Nightreign wiki, IGN, Game8 — examples:  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Beast  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Old+Pocketwatch  
  https://www.ign.com/wikis/elden-ring-nightreign/Tricephalos_-_Gladius,_Beast_of_Night_Boss_Guide

2) Adel, Baron of Night (a.k.a. Gaping Jaw)  
- Short description: Massive, wide‑mouthed draconic/monstrous Nightlord that uses long reach bites, gravity/lightning‑tinged area attacks and heavy telegraphed lunges.  
- First‑clear relic: Night of the Baron (first‑clear relic reward).  
- Main weakness: Poison/status (primary). (No single strong elemental; Poison/status builds are the most effective.)  
- Sources: Fandom / Fextralife / IGN guides:  
  https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Night_of_the_Baron  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Adel+Baron+of+Night

3) Gnoster, Wisdom of Night (a.k.a. Sentient Pest)  
- Short description: Multi‑part pest/swarm Nightlord (moth/scorpion‑style pairing) combining ranged magic, status application and multi‑part attacks; fights emphasize handling parts/swarms.  
- First‑clear relic: Night of the Wise (unique relic awarded on first defeat).  
- Main weakness: Fire (primary).  
- Sources: Fextralife / IGN / Game8:  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Wise  
  https://www.ign.com/wikis/elden-ring-nightreign/Sentient_Pest_-_Gnoster,_Wisdom_of_Night_Boss_Guide

4) Maris, Fathom of Night (a.k.a. Augur)  
- Short description: Eldritch/astral Augur Nightlord that channels large global spells and sleep/sorcery effects; the fight involves interrupt windows and cosmic‑style attacks.  
- First‑clear relic: Dark Night of the Fathom (relic unlocked/added to the Collector Signboard after first clear — not necessarily a one‑off inventory drop).  
- Main weakness: Lightning (primary).  
- Sources: Fextralife / TheGamer / Game8:  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Maris+Fathom+of+Night  
  https://www.thegamer.com/elden-ring-nightreign-augur-maris-nightlord-boss-battle-tips-strategy-guide/

5) Libra, Creature of Night (a.k.a. Equilibrious Beast)  
- Short description: Horned/ritualistic humanoid Nightlord that mixes close physical strikes with madness‑inducing occult incantations; fight pressures status/posture.  
- First‑clear relic: Dark Night of the Demon (relic becomes available/unlocked for purchase from the Collector Signboard after first clear).  
- Main weakness: Madness (status) is the most effective counter (status‑based weakness rather than a single elemental). Holy/Fire are useful secondary options.  
- Sources: Fextralife / TheGamer / Game8:  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Dark+Night+of+the+Demon  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Libra+Creature+of+Night

6) Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow (a.k.a. Darkdrift Knight)  
- Short description: Heavy, long‑reach mounted/centaur‑style knight with sweeping sword slashes, charge attacks and multi‑phase arm‑regeneration mechanics.  
- First‑clear relic: Night of the Champion (unique relic awarded on first clear).  
- Main weakness: Lightning (primary).  
- Sources: Fextralife / IGN / Game8:  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Champion  
  https://www.ign.com/wikis/elden-ring-nightreign/Darkdrift_Knight_-_Fulghor,_Champion_of_Nightglow_Boss_Guide

7) Caligo, Miasma of Night (a.k.a. Fissure in the Fog)  
- Short description: Dragon‑style Nightlord with frostbreath, fog/miasma area denial and frostbite mechanics; resembles large draconic Everlasting forms but with fog/rot theme.  
- First‑clear relic: Dark Night of the Miasma (relic unlocked/added to Collector Signboard after first clear).  
- Main weakness: Fire (primary).  
- Sources: Fextralife / wiki.gg / PC Gamer / Shacknews:  
  https://eldenring.wiki.gg/wiki/Nightreign:Dark_Night_of_the_Miasma  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Caligo+Miasma+of+Night

8) Heolstor the Nightlord (a.k.a. Night Aspect / The Shape of Night)  
- Short description: Spectral / primordial humanoid Night Aspect with reality‑warping telegraphed strikes and multiple phase transitions; cinematic, varied patterns.  
- First‑clear relic: Night of the Lord (unique relic dropped/awarded on first clear).  
- Main weakness: Holy (primary). (Lightning can be a useful secondary in later phases.)  
- Sources: Fextralife / wiki.gg / Game8:  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night+of+the+Lord  
  https://eldenring.wiki.gg/wiki/Heolstor_The_Nightlord

Forsaken Hollows (DLC) Nightlords

9) Weapon‑Bequeathed Harmonia (a.k.a. Balancers)  
- Short description: Choreographed squad boss (Valkyrie‑like group) that uses coordinated strikes and cleansing weapon purges; encounter rewards crowd control and status exploitation.  
- First‑clear relic: The Will of the Balancers (unique relic received on first clear).  
- Main weakness: Sleep (status) — they are most susceptible to Sleep rather than a standard element; no meaningful single elemental weakness (they have partial resistance to many elements).  
- Sources: IGN / Fextralife / TheGamer / GamesRadar:  
  https://www.ign.com/wikis/elden-ring-nightreign/Balancers_-_Weapon-Bequeathed_Harmonia_Boss_Guide  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapon+Bequeathed+Harmonia

10) Traitorous Straghess (a.k.a. Dreglord)  
- Short description: Massive reconstituting dreg mound/corpse‑colossus that regenerates parts, spreads rot and fights as a sprawling multi‑phase boss.  
- First‑clear relic: The Night of Dregs (unique relic awarded on first clear).  
- Main weakness: Fire (primary). Holy is also effective (secondary). Be prepared for Scar‑Rot mechanics.  
- Sources: IGN / Fextralife / Fandom:  
  https://www.ign.com/wikis/elden-ring-nightreign/Dreglord_-_Traitorous_Straghess_Boss_Guide  
  https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Traitorous+Straghess

Notes, caveats and next steps
- “Main weakness” above is the single most commonly recommended damage type or status to exploit in community and guide sources. Several Nightlords are primarily weak to status effects (Poison, Madness, Sleep) rather than a classic elemental like Fire/Lightning/Holy — I labeled those appropriately.  
- Some relics are given as immediate first‑clear drops/rewards; others are “unlocked” and become available from the Collector Signboard (shop) after you defeat the Nightlord the first time. I noted that where guides indicate it.  
- There are tougher Everdark Sovereign variants and weekly rot/variant forms for many Nightlords; weaknesses can shift slightly in those variants. The links above include more detailed resistance tables and phase notes where applicable.

Nightlords

Below is a clear, consolidated report for every Nightlord in Elden Ring: Nightreign (base game + Forsaken Hollows DLC) showing: boss name and where encountered, the unique Nightlord relic(s) tied to their first defeat, a short description/effects of each relic, whether it’s a one-time unique unlock or an immediate drop, and the Nightlord’s main elemental weakness plus notable status vulnerabilities.

Summary / quick list of Nightlords covered
- Base game (8): Gladius, Beast of Night; Adel, Baron of Night; Gnoster, Wisdom of Night; Maris, Fathom of Night; Libra, Creature of Night; Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow; Caligo, Miasma of Night; Heolstor the Nightlord.  
- Forsaken Hollows DLC (2): Weapon‑Bequeathed Harmonia; Traitorous Straghess.

Detailed entries

1) Gladius, Beast of Night
- Encounter: Tricephalos expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic(s) on first defeat: Night of the Beast; Old Pocketwatch.
  - Night of the Beast — flavor: “The night belonging to Gladius…”. Reported mechanical effects: stamina recovery on successful attacks, melee starting weapon gains fire properties / attack tweaks (community listings differ on exact numbers). 
  - Old Pocketwatch — flavor: small utility relic; reported effects include FP restoration on successive attacks and a small Dexterity bonus.
- One-time unique? Both are unique boss relic unlocks tied to the first clear (the first victory grants these named relic rewards / unlocks).
- Main elemental weakness: Holy (strongest/easiest elemental to exploit).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Sleep is effective vs. Gladius; other status types (Bleed/Rot/Frost) are not specially effective.

2) Adel, Baron of Night
- Encounter: Gaping Jaw expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: Night of the Baron.
  - Effects (reported): bonuses tied to critical hits (improved criticals / stamina or art-gauge interactions per guide listings); flavor text: “The night belonging to Adel…”.
- One-time unique? Yes — unique relic awarded / unlocked at first defeat (Everdark variant has its own separate relic afterward).
- Main elemental weakness: Poison (poison buildup is especially effective in phase 1).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Best exploited early with Poison; becomes more resistant later (gains Lightning properties in later phases).

3) Gnoster, Wisdom of Night
- Encounter: Sentient Pest expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: Night of the Wise.
  - Effects (reported): increases maximum FP; starting armament inflicts poison; interactions that boost attack when poison/rot is present (wiki/community summaries).
- One-time unique? Yes — unique relic awarded/unlocked on first clear.
- Main elemental weakness: Fire (fire damage recommended).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Vulnerable to Scarlet Rot, Blood Loss (bleed) and Frostbite in some phases/contexts; poison mechanics appear in the fight.

4) Maris, Fathom of Night
- Encounter: Augur expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: Dark Night of the Fathom (often shortened to Night of the Fathom in guides).
  - Effects (reported): increases maximum HP, grants continuous/periodic HP recovery and passive team healing effects when low HP (community/wikis list these healing-oriented bonuses).
- One-time unique? Yes — unique relic unlock on first clear (then becomes obtainable via the relic/collector system).
- Main elemental weakness: Lightning (staggered/broken most readily by Lightning).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Boss inflicts Sleep (watch out); Lightning is best tool to interrupt channels/hypnosis.

5) Libra, Creature of Night
- Encounter: Equilibrious Beast expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic: Dark Night of the Demon (associated with Libra).
  - Effects (reported): bonuses that interact with Madness (Madness-building mechanics and FP recovery interactions), increases damage when taking attacks, etc.
- One-time unique? Important distinction: community reports indicate Libra’s named relic is tied to defeating the Everdark Sovereign variant — it is unlocked for purchase via the Collector signboard after that sovereign defeat rather than always being an immediate corpse drop on base encounter. In short: defeating the Everdark / sovereign variant unlocks the relic for collection/purchase; some base clears may not immediately drop the relic in inventory.
- Main elemental weakness: Holy and Fire are effective; Libra is especially vulnerable to Madness-building mechanics.
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Highly susceptible to Madness buildup; Sleep immunity is commonly reported; bleed/rot are not primary.

6) Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow
- Encounter: Darkdrift Knight expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: Dark Night of the Champion (sometimes shortened to Night of the Champion in some guides).
  - Effects (reported): increases maximum Stamina, boosts attack power of added affinity attacks, modestly increases art-gauge fill on kills (community/wikis differ on exact numbers).
- One-time unique? Yes — unlocks on first clear (then available via collector system / relic menu).
- Main elemental weakness: Lightning (Lightning affinity and lightning attacks stagger/interrupt well).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Susceptible to Poison and Scarlet Rot (Scarlet Rot often recommended), and is affected by Bleed/Frostbite; reported resistant to Holy and immune to Madness.

7) Caligo, Miasma of Night
- Encounter: Fissure in the Fog expedition (third-night Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: Dark Night of the Miasma.
  - Effects (reported): adds frost properties to starting armament, nearby frost interactions (concealment/benefit) and physical-damage mitigation adjustments (community summaries).
- One-time unique? Yes — unlocks on first defeat and becomes available normally afterward from the collector/shop system.
- Main elemental weakness: Fire (fire damage recommended).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Bleed is reported as an effective status to apply; Caligo itself uses Frostbite attacks (so prepare frost resistance).

8) Heolstor the Nightlord
- Encounter: Night Aspect expedition (third-night Nightlord) — the “primordial” Nightlord form.
- Unique relic on first defeat: Night of the Lord.
  - Effects (reported): adds weapon affinity-style bonuses (e.g., switching weapons grants added affinity attack and boosts that attack’s power), flavor text: “The night belonging to Heolstor…” etc.
- One-time unique? Yes — unique boss relic unlocked on first defeat (then available through the relic/collector system).
- Main elemental weakness: Holy (overall best element); Fire can be useful vs early forms and Lightning can be a secondary option in certain phases.
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Some susceptibility to Frostbite and Scarlet Rot in certain conditions; resistant to Bleed.

9) Weapon‑Bequeathed Harmonia (Forsaken Hollows DLC)
- Encounter: Balancers expedition (DLC Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: The Will of the Balancers.
  - Effects (reported): improved melee attack power and skill attack power, and continuous/slow FP recovery perks (community/wiki effect summaries).
- One-time unique? Yes — unique boss relic unlock on first clear.
- Main elemental weakness: Sleep (they are particularly vulnerable to Sleep/status-sleep interactions).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Resistant to damage-over-time like Bleed and Frost; Sleep is primary exploit.

10) Traitorous Straghess (Forsaken Hollows DLC)
- Encounter: Dreglord expedition (DLC Nightlord).
- Unique relic on first defeat: The Night of Dregs.
  - Effects (reported): status-ailment stacking increases attack power, inflicts/augments Scarlet Rot effects, and rot-proximity continuous heals or similar rot-related interactions (community/wikis list specifics).
- One-time unique? Yes — unique relic awarded/unlocked on first clear (then available through relic/collector channels).
- Main elemental weakness: Fire and Holy (both effective).
- Notable status vulnerabilities: Susceptible to Frostbite and Bleed; the boss itself uses Scarlet Rot extensively so bring preservative items for survivability.

Notes, caveats, and sources
- Wording and numeric effect values in relic descriptions vary slightly among community wikis (Fextralife, Nightreign / Elden Ring Nightreign wikis, Game8, Mobalytics). In this report I quoted consolidated, commonly reported effect descriptions; exact numeric bonuses (e.g., +HP, +stamina numbers, exact FP/HP/sec) may differ in specific database entries — if you want exact in-game tooltip text I can extract the precise wording / numbers for every relic.
- “One-time unique?” — in Nightreign, defeating a Nightlord for the first time normally unlocks that Nightlord’s named relic. In many cases it is added to your inventory or becomes unlocked for purchase via the Collector signboard; some sovereign/everdark variants are specifically required to unlock certain relics for purchase. I noted where the community commonly reports that nuance (e.g., Libra’s relic is commonly tied to defeating the Everdark Sovereign variant to unlock).
- If you want, I can: (a) extract exact in‑game relic tooltip text for each relic (verbatim); (b) provide the Collector-signboard unlock conditions and sovereign-sigil costs where applicable; (c) give recommended items/armor/consumables and fast strategies to exploit the listed weaknesses for each boss; (d) provide direct links to the wiki pages used as source references.

all_scores.question: Você pode fazer um relatório sobre todos os chefes de lembrança de Elden Ring considerando tanto o jogo base quanto o DLC? Quero saber todas as recompensas que podem ser trocadas por cada lembrança.
all_scores.response:
Below is a consolidated, ready-to-use report of every Remembrance boss (base game + Shadow of the Erdtree DLC) and exactly what Finger Reader Enia will offer in exchange for each Remembrance. For each boss I list: 1) the exact Remembrance item name you receive, 2) every Enia trade option (reward name + item type), and 3) short special notes (one-time choices, duplication, small extra rune costs, or other behavior).

Quick reminders before the list
- Trading a Remembrance to Enia consumes it and grants the chosen reward. To get both/all choices from one Remembrance you must first duplicate it at a Walking Mausoleum / Remembrance Duplication Coffin (one duplication opportunity per Mausoleum).  
- Alternatively you can consume a Remembrance for runes instead of trading it (large rune values; varies by Remembrance).  
- Most Enia trades require only the Remembrance. A few community reports note small additional rune payments for certain spirit-ash trades in some versions — if Enia’s dialog asks for runes, you must pay them.  
- DLC final Remembrance(s) may offer three choices (not just two). The Heart of Bayle (DLC) is a special non-Remembrance item that behaves similarly but is not traded at Enia — noted at the end.

BASE GAME Remembrances (names & Enia trade options)
1) Boss: Godrick the Grafted
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Grafted
- Enia trade options:
  - Axe of Godrick — weapon (axe)
  - Grafted Dragon — weapon (fist)
- Notes: standard two-choice Remembrance.

2) Boss: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen
- Enia trade options:
  - Carian Regal Scepter — weapon (staff)
  - Rennala’s Full Moon — sorcery
- Notes: Rennala’s Full Moon is a powerful sorcery.

3) Boss: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Blasphemous
- Enia trade options:
  - Rykard’s Rancour — sorcery
  - Blasphemous Blade — weapon (greatsword)
- Notes: the pair is sorcery + unique weapon.

4) Boss: Starscourge Radahn
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Starscourge
- Enia trade options:
  - Starscourge Greatsword — weapon (greatsword)
  - Lion Greatbow — weapon (greatbow)
- Notes: two powerful weapon options.

5) Boss: Morgott, the Omen King
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Omen King
- Enia trade options:
  - Morgott’s Cursed Sword — weapon (curved greatsword-like unique)
  - Regal Omen Bairn — spirit ash
- Notes: some reports note a small rune cost for particular spirit-ash trades in some versions; if Enia’s dialog requests runes, pay it. Otherwise standard two-choice trade.

6) Boss: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Naturalborn
- Enia trade options:
  - Bastard’s Stars — weapon (flail-type unique)
  - Ash of War: Wave of Darkness — ash of war (weapon skill)
- Notes: Wave of Darkness is an Ash of War choice.

7) Boss: Lichdragon Fortissax
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Lichdragon
- Enia trade options:
  - Fortissax’s Lightning Spear — incantation
  - Death Lightning — incantation
- Notes: both are powerful incantations.

8) Boss: Fire Giant
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Fire Giant
- Enia trade options:
  - Giant’s Red Braid — weapon (whip)
  - Burn, O Flame! — incantation
- Notes: standard two-choice Remembrance.

9) Boss: Dragonlord Placidusax
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Dragonlord
- Enia trade options:
  - Dragon King’s Cragblade — weapon (unique heavy thrusting/colossal-style)
  - Placidusax’s Ruin — incantation
- Notes: both unique DLC-like items but in base game content.

10) Boss: Maliketh, the Black Blade
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Black Blade
- Enia trade options:
  - Maliketh’s Black Blade — weapon (colossal sword)
  - Black Blade — incantation
- Notes: iconic two-option Remembrance.

11) Boss: Mohg, Lord of Blood
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Blood Lord
- Enia trade options:
  - Mohgwyn’s Sacred Spear — weapon (great spear)
  - Bloodboon — incantation
- Notes: standard two choices (weapon + incantation).

12) Boss: Hoarah Loux (Godfrey, First Elden Lord — warrior form)
- Remembrance: Remembrance of Hoarah Loux
- Enia trade options:
  - Axe of Godfrey — weapon (colossal/large axe)
  - Ash of War: Hoarah Loux’s Earthshaker — ash of war (weapon skill)
- Notes: Earthshaker is an Ash of War.

13) Boss: Regal Ancestor Spirit
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Regal Ancestor
- Enia trade options:
  - Winged Greathorn — weapon (greataxe)
  - Ancestral Spirit’s Horn — talisman (unique talisman-like item)
- Notes: Ancestral Spirit’s Horn is a unique talisman/spirit-related item.

14) Boss: Malenia, Goddess of Rot
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Rot Goddess
- Enia trade options:
  - Scarlet Aeonia — incantation
  - Hand of Malenia — weapon (katana)
- Notes: extremely sought-after choices; many players duplicate this Remembrance to claim both.

15) Boss: Elden Beast
- Remembrance: Elden Remembrance
- Enia trade options:
  - Marika’s Hammer — weapon (hammer)
  - Sacred Relic Sword — weapon (greatsword / unique)
- Notes: the “Elden Remembrance” behaves like other Remembrances; choose carefully.

SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE (DLC) Remembrances
(Each named DLC boss drops a Remembrance of X — take that to Enia at Roundtable Hold for the listed options.)

1) Boss: Divine Beast Dancing Lion
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Dancing Lion
- Enia trade options:
  - Enraged Divine Beast — talisman
  - Divine Beast Frost Stomp — ash of war
- Notes: both are DLC-unique.

2) Boss: Rellana, Twin Moon Knight
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Twin Moon Knight
- Enia trade options:
  - Rellana’s Twin Blades — weapon (unique dual-blade/light greatsword-style)
  - Rellana’s Twin Moons — sorcery
- Notes: major DLC weapon + sorcery pair.

3) Boss: Messmer the Impaler
- Remembrance: Remembrance of the Impaler
- Enia trade options:
  - Spear of the Impaler — weapon (great spear with unique effects)
  - Messmer’s Orb — incantation
- Notes: DLC-unique spear and incantation.
